# Headent Client 1.0.6

Teletext is here — decoded by the app itself, so it works over HTSP **and** HTTP, on
TV boxes with a remote and on phones by touch. Favourites can now be reordered by
dragging on the phone, and the app was moved to the new Android build tools with a
much better optimized release build. Available on
**[Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=sk.tvhclient)**.

## What's new

- **Teletext** — a complete EBU teletext decoder (EN 300 706) built into the app.
  Colour text, mosaic graphics, double height, subpages, Fastext colour links and the
  live rolling header with the broadcaster's clock. Pages are collected in the
  background while you watch, so most of them open instantly.
  - **Works in both connection modes.** Over HTSP the teletext stream is read from the
    subscription; over HTTP the app opens a short second connection to the same channel
    while teletext is open.
  - **All European character sets** — Latin with 13 national subsets (Czech/Slovak,
    Polish, German, French, Italian, Spanish/Portuguese, Turkish, Romanian,
    Serbian/Croatian/Slovenian, Estonian, Lithuanian/Latvian, Swedish/Finnish/Hungarian,
    English), Cyrillic (Russian/Bulgarian, Ukrainian, Serbian), Greek and Hebrew,
    including the X/28 and M/29 packets that broadcasters use to select them.
  - **On TV:** *Teletext* in the *More* menu (modern mode) or in the control bar
    (classic mode). 0–9 picks a page, ▲▼ move page by page, ◀▶ switch subpages,
    OK toggles the transparent overlay, the colour buttons follow Fastext links,
    INFO reveals hidden characters (quizzes), BACK closes.
  - **On phones:** a touch bar with a keypad for the page number, subpage arrows,
    transparency and close; tap the top or bottom half of the page to move page by page.
  - Teletext is offered only for live channels that actually broadcast it.
- **Reorder favourites by dragging (phone)** — in the *Favourites* group every row has
  a handle on the right; drag it to move the channel. The order is saved immediately and
  is the same order the player, the TV and the home screen use.
- **Favourite channels are marked** — a star next to channels that are in your
  favourites, visible in *All channels* and in tag groups (list, grid and tiles).
- **Radio catches up with Channels** — the *Radio* tab has the same *Favourites* filter
  chip (remembered per server), a star on favourite stations, a marker on hidden ones,
  and on phones favourite stations can be reordered by dragging as well. On TV, the player
  offers the *Favourites* and *Hidden* groups for radio too (hold OK), including
  *Reorder favourites*.
- **Radio stations numbered from 1** — stations are numbered 1, 2, 3… in the order shown
  (per group) instead of the server's numbers, which for radio are rarely meaningful. Applies
  to the Radio tab, the guide and the station list in the player; entering a number on the
  remote follows it. *Settings → Appearance → Radio* switches it off to show the server
  numbers again.
- **TV guide for radio** — the *Radio* tab has the same guide button as the channel list and
  opens the grid with the stations and their own groups; in the channel guide, *Radio* is
  one more entry in the group filter. Radio stations were previously left out of the guide
  entirely. Starting a programme plays the station as radio (mini player on the phone).
  On TV, the guide key pressed while a radio station is playing opens the guide at the
  stations, not at the TV channels.
- **Favourites as launcher shortcuts** — the app publishes your favourite channels (up
  to 8, in your order) as Android app shortcuts with the channel's picon as the icon.
  On a phone, long-press the app icon to see them; on Android TV, launchers that show
  app shortcuts (for example Projectivity) list them as tiles. Tapping one opens the
  player directly on that channel. The stock Google TV launcher does not display app
  shortcuts, so nothing changes there.
- **Favourites row on the Android TV home screen** — the app publishes a *Favourites*
  row next to the ones from Netflix or YouTube: one 16:9 tile per favourite channel with
  its picon, and beneath it the current programme ("Now: … · 20:15 – 21:00") and the
  next one. OK opens the player on that channel. The system asks once whether to add the
  row; it updates whenever the app runs (favourites change, channel list loads). The
  stock Google TV home shows app rows differently, so there it may look reduced.
- **Deep link to a channel** — `headentclient://channel/<uuid>` opens the player on
  that channel, from any launcher, automation app or `adb shell am start -a
  android.intent.action.VIEW -d "headentclient://channel/<uuid>"`.
- **Media keys on TV remotes** — STOP ends playback, PLAY/PAUSE and PLAY-PAUSE control
  the pause, REWIND/FAST FORWARD jump 30 s in recordings and in the timeshift buffer,
  NEXT/PREVIOUS switch channels (in a recording they jump a minute). On Google TV
  remotes the *bookmark* key adds or removes the current channel from favourites and the
  *live TV* key opens the channel list (or returns to live TV from a recording), where the
  system passes those keys to apps.
- **Open a channel full screen with a single OK** — a new option under *Settings → Remote
  control*. By default the first OK in the player's channel list switches the channel behind
  the open list and a second one closes the list; with the option on, one OK starts the
  channel full screen straight away. Holding OK still opens the channel menu, and it works
  the same in modern and classic mode.
- **TV Channels tile can open the list first (TV)** — a new option under *Settings →
  Appearance → Home screen (TV)*. With it on, the tile on the home screen opens the player with
  the channel list already open and nothing playing; the channel starts once you pick one, and
  BACK from the list returns to the home screen. Off by default (the tile starts the last
  channel, as before).
- **Choose the recording profile per recording** — *Settings → Playback → Ask for the recording
  profile*. With it on, *Record* first shows the server's DVR profiles (storage folder, retention…)
  and records into the one you pick, remembering it for next time. Shown only when the server
  offers more than one profile; cancelling a recording never asks. Off by default — recordings
  go to the profile set for the server, as before.
- **The player follows the group you picked** — starting a channel from the phone hands
  the player exactly the group selected in the list (Favourites, a tag, or all channels),
  so CH+/− and the in-player list stay inside it.

## What's fixed

- **Switching between HTTP and HTSP mid-session** — the channel list is reloaded
  immediately, so *Watch* on the home screen works without opening the channel list
  first; the recording dots stay visible, and the saved "last channel" from the other
  mode is no longer used (channel identifiers differ between the two modes).
- **Missing now/next for some channels over HTSP** — channels for which the server
  returns nothing without a time window are asked again with one, and an incomplete
  result is no longer remembered as fresh for three hours. When the HTSP connection
  drops in the middle of the now/next pass, the app reconnects and continues instead
  of marking every remaining channel as failed; a failed connection is retried three times
  (mobile networks occasionally fail a DNS lookup for a second); retries back off (20 s, 60 s, 3 min).
- **No programme information in the Radio tab** — radio stations showed only their name.
  The station list now gets the same "now playing" line, progress bar and *Next* as the
  channel list: over HTTP the now/next data is read together with the station list, and
  over HTSP the Radio tab now starts the now/next pass itself instead of relying on the
  Channels tab having been opened first. On TV the player's radio list gets it too.
- **The guide opened at the first channel** — opening the TV guide from the player now
  starts on the channel (or radio station) you are watching, with the cursor on its current
  programme, instead of jumping to the top of the list. That channel is marked in the
  channel column, and on a phone (where the grid has no cursor) the programme on air is
  highlighted as well, so it is clear where you are starting from.
- **Playback stopping by itself on servers that allow one connection per user** — while a
  channel or a recording was playing over HTSP, the app could open a second connection in
  the background (now/next, recordings list). Servers configured with a connection limit of
  one per user refused it and dropped the connection that was playing, so playback stopped
  after a while and reconnected in a loop. Background queries are now skipped while a stream
  is running and use the data already cached; they run again once playback ends — a skipped
  now/next pass is not reported as an error in the diagnostic log and is not retried while
  the stream is running; the Channels tab picks it up once playback stops.
- **Moving the position in a recording** — with a remote, ◀ ▶ used to jump immediately
  (and by different amounts, 15 s back but 30 s forward), so the picture froze on every
  press and while the button was held. Now the arrows move a marker on the progress bar in
  30 s steps — including from a hidden control bar and while holding the button — and the
  jump itself happens once, after the button is released (two seconds after the last press),
  or immediately on OK — the movement is never interrupted while the button is held. Holding
  an arrow moves the marker smoothly and speeds up the longer it is held; the speed also
  scales with the length of the recording, so a six-hour one is crossed in about ten seconds
  rather than a minute. Ending up back where playback already is does not restart the
  stream at all.
- **Seeking near the end of a recording could stop playback** — the recording's length
  comes from the programme data, and the file is often a little shorter, so a jump close to
  the end landed past the end of the file and the player simply stopped. Jumps now keep a
  short reserve, and if a jump still lands past the end, the player steps back and continues
  instead of stopping.
- **Leaving the home screen while the last channel was still loading** — on a TV box the app
  restores the channel you were watching, and that wait continued even if you moved to the
  archive, the guide or the settings in the meantime; when the channel list finally arrived,
  the player opened over the screen you had moved to, the app stuttered and could crash.
  Moving away now cancels the pending playback.
- **A small picture flashed in the corner after switching a channel (TV)** — with the channel
  list open the video plays in a small preview, and the video surface needs a moment to grow
  back to full screen when the list closes, so a new channel started inside the small
  rectangle and the picture appeared tiny in the corner first. With the single-OK option the
  channel now starts once the picture is back at full size.
- **Refreshing the archive looked like nothing happened** — the reload keeps the current
  list while it fetches, so with an unchanged archive there was no sign it had run. The
  button now turns into a spinner while loading (phone and TV) and says so when the
  refresh fails and the old list is kept.
- **Archive list failing on a dropped connection** — when the server closed an idle
  connection or the phone switched between Wi-Fi and mobile data, the recordings list
  reported an error ("Software caused connection abort"). The first such failure is now
  retried once, quietly; leaving the screen mid-load is no longer recorded as an error.
- **Channel list opening in the middle or at the end (phone)** — the jump to the last
  watched channel is now done only on Android TV, where the remote needs the focus
  there. On phones and tablets both the Channels and the Radio tab open at the top.
- **Teletext on phones in landscape** — the page no longer stretches across the whole
  width of a tall (20:9) display; the cell aspect is capped and the page is centred.
  On 16:9 TVs nothing changes.
- **Picture-in-picture on TV boxes** — some Android TV devices report PiP support, so
  BACK during playback shrank the video into a floating window that cannot be focused or
  closed with a remote. Automatic PiP is now off by default on TV (BACK stops playback)
  and the PiP button is not offered there; it can still be enabled in Settings. The PiP
  window on TV also gained a *Close* action next to play/pause (it appears in the system's
  PiP menu, where the box offers one; phones already have the system's own close button), and while the window is showing, the remote's media
  keys reach it directly: STOP closes it, PLAY/PAUSE toggles, and holding PLAY/PAUSE closes
  it too — for remotes that have only that one media button.
- **Gestures under an open menu** — swiping while *More*, *Audio*, *Subtitles*,
  *Profile* or the sleep timer was open changed the volume, pulled out the channel list
  or switched channels behind it. Menus now consume the gesture.
- **Panel widths** — the *More* menu and the sleep timer are centred dialogs of the same
  width as the audio/subtitle picker instead of stretching across the screen; on a phone
  in landscape the *More* sheet is narrower and scrolls.
- **Modern mode polish** — the audio/subtitle/profile picker follows the modern theme,
  and *Teletext* has its own icon in the *More* menu.

## Under the hood

- **Android Gradle Plugin 9.3, Gradle 9.5, Kotlin 2.3** — the shared module now uses
  the new Kotlin Multiplatform Android library plugin and the app uses AGP's built-in
  Kotlin support.
- **Gradle wrapper included** — `./gradlew` (Gradle 9.5.0) is part of the repository, so the
  project opens in Android Studio and builds from a fresh clone without installing Gradle.
- **Smaller, better optimized release build** — the blanket "keep everything" R8 rules
  for Ktor, the shared module and Tink were replaced by targeted ones, so code shrinking,
  optimization and obfuscation now cover most of the app instead of half of it.

## Known issues

- Teletext is available for live channels; teletext subtitles (page 888) are not yet
  used as a subtitle source.
- Arabic teletext is displayed in the Latin character set (letter shaping and
  right-to-left layout are not implemented).
- Not every broadcaster still transmits teletext, and some public broadcasters leave it
  out of their satellite feed while keeping it on terrestrial or cable. The app offers
  teletext only when the stream actually carries it.
- Launcher shortcuts for favourites cover TV channels; radio favourites are not published
  yet.
- On older 32-bit boxes, 1080p50 10-bit HEVC channels may still stutter over HTSP.
  Using the HTTP streaming path with the `pass` profile works around it.
- Timeshift is an HTSP feature; it is not available over the HTTP path.

## Which APK do I need?

- **Most TV boxes and phones (64-bit):** `HeadentClient-1.0.6-arm64-v8a.apk`
- **Older 32-bit devices:** `HeadentClient-1.0.6-armeabi-v7a.apk`
- **Not sure?** `HeadentClient-1.0.6-universal.apk` works everywhere
  (larger download).

Google Play picks the right variant automatically.
